STEP 1 - Scene: A snack-sized portion of roasted/raw almonds on a white plate. Not a full meal.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White paper or plastic plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side plate). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds (shelled, brown skins on), about 30-35 nuts.

STEP 4 - Area: Almonds cover roughly 25% of the plate's inner area (the pile sits in the central region, with clear rim visible). Almonds 25% ≈ 79 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile is about 2 almonds deep in the center, so typical height ~1.5 cm. 79 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 118 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds are dense nuts with air gaps between pieces; bulk density for whole nuts is around 0.5-0.6 g/ml. 118 ml x 0.55 ≈ 65 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw almonds ≈ 579 kcal/100 g. 65 g x 5.79 ≈ 376 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 30-35 almonds weighing ~65 g is plausible (a single almond is ~1.2 g, so 35 almonds ≈ 42 g; 65 g implies somewhat more nuts or larger ones, so I'll settle near 55 g as a compromise). Recalculated: 55 g x 5.79 ≈ 318 kcal. Total is a modest, plausible snack.
